entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1. Present petition has been filed with the prayer to revise the award dated 05.09.2017 bearing LAQ Case No. NHAI/18/2013 for Vadodara - Mumbai Express Way / Kanthariya Compensation Case NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined and to recompute the compensation for the lands belonging to the petitioners by multiplying the market value as determined under Section 26(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, "LARR Act, 2013") with Factor-2 and applying all other statutory benefits as provided under the LARR Act, 2013 including the benefits of solatium and interest etc. under Section 30 of the said LARR Act with the statutory interest payable thereon.
2.

When the matter was argued on 07.11.2023, Mr. Maulik G. Nanavati, learned advocate appearing for the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) though did not dispute any claim of the petitioners for seeking revision of the award by applying Factor-2 in terms of Section 26(1) of the LARR Act, 2013, however, a dispute was raised with regard to the discrepancy in the record of the writ petition about the area of the acquired land of Survey No. 182/6.

From various documents on record of the writ petition, it was sought to be agitated by the learned advocate appearing for the NHAI that in view of the discrepancy in the total area of Survey No. 182/6, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined showing in the revenue records, it would be difficult for the respondents to apply Factor-2 for recomputation of the compensation for the acquired land in question.

3. Noticing the said controversy, we required the counsel for the NHAI and the learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondent No. 1 to file affidavits of the competent authority to bring before us the correct position with regard to the acquired area of Survey No. 182/6, subject matter of consideration herein.
The revenue records pertaining to the land in question was also required to be examined by the competent authority and the material was to be placed.
The NHAI was also directed to make an inquiry at its end.
However, we may record that no affidavit of NHAI has been filed in compliance of the said order.

In the affidavit filed on behalf of the State respondent namely the respondent No. 1, it is stated in paragraph 3 therein that the total area of the land bearing Survey No. 182/6 was admeasuring about 14062 sq. mtrs., situated at Village:
Kanthariya, Taluka and District: Bharuch.

The said land came to be partitioned by way of family arrangement, whereby, 1 acre and 30 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined gunthas of the land in question came under the ownership of one Hasanali Ismail, whereas, 1 acre and 29 gunthas came to be owned by heirs of Ahemad Ali.

The Mutation Entry No. 3221 reflecting the partition of the land in question by way of family arrangement came to be certified in the Village Form No. 6 on 12.12.1986, the copy whereof, has been appended as Annexure 'R-1' to the affidavit of the respondent No. 1.

It is then stated in paragraph 4 of the said affidavit that the partition of the land in question came to be reflected only in the revenue records, however, the same has not been reflected into the records of the office of the District Inspector of Land Records (DILR),

sentences.text: Bharuch
. As a result, controversy arose about the area of Survey No. 182/6, which has been raised on behalf of the NHAI.

However, it is further clarified that vide Notification dated 06.08.2013 under Section 3(A) of the National Highways Act,
1956, land in Survey No. 182/6, admeasuring 8640 sq. mtrs. came to be acquired.
The NHAI, while preparation of the land acquisition record, had relied upon the records of DILR, which did not contain the description with regard to the partition of the land in question.

The Notification under Section 3(D) dated 25.07.2014 also contains NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined the description of the acquired land as Survey No. 182/6, admeasuring 8640 sq. mtrs.

The result is that an award dated 27.06.2017 under Section 3(G) of the National Highways Act, 1956 was declared reflecting the acquired land in Survey No.
182/6 in the ownership of Hasanali, Inayat Yakub.

It is further stated that the award erroneously reflected the area of Survey No. 182/6 as 7082 sq. mtrs. and it is clear from the Notification published by the NHAI that the total area of acquired land in Survey No. 182/6 was 8640 sq. mtrs.
4.

An order dated 03.05.2019 passed by the Competent Authority (NHAI), Bharuch and Deputy Collector, Ankleshwar, has been passed at the stage of disbursement of compensation to the holders of the land in question.

The copy of the order dated 03.05.2019 placed on record, has been shown to us to demonstrate that the said order records the following facts:
"8

It is stated that the office of the Answering Respondent has passed an order dated 03.05.2019, whereby, the amount of compensation came to be disbursed to the to be entitled land holders of the land in question.
It is stated that the land bearing survey No. 182/6 (New Survey No. 688) admeasuring about 9309 Sq. Mtrs. out of which 4440 Sq. Mtrs. had been acquired;

(iii) The re-measurement of the land in question on 6.4.2019 highlights the fact that the Revenue Survey no. 182/6-1 (New Survey No. 702) reflects the name of the heirs of Inayat Yakub ali and Ikramul Yakub Ali as Occupier.

entities.text: Sajid Ismail Hasan Ali vs Competent Authority, National Highway
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) It is stated that 8640 Sq. Mtrs. of the land in question had been acquired for the acquisition project.
The concerned land owners had been paid the compensation in accordance with the land laws by their acquisition proceedings.

The Copies of the order dated 03.05.2019 along with the measurement sheet dated 6.4.2019 and resultant Form No. 4 prepared by the office of DILR,
Bharuch, are annexed herewith and marked as Annexure R.5 (Colly.)."
5.

From the careful perusal of the order of disbursement dated NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined 03.05.2019, it is evident that the compensation was disbursed amongst the land owners of Survey No. 182/6 recording the factum of family partition amongst them.

However, the fact remains that the compensation paid to the land owners was for the total area of 8640 sq. mtrs., of Survey No. 182/6, acquired by the NHAI.
6.
The dispute, thus, is sought to be raised before us about the area of the acquired land, is misconceived.

We, therefore, reject the contention of Mr. Maulik G. Nanavati, learned advocate appearing for the respondent - NHAI that in view of the dispute pertaining to the correct area of Survey No. 182/6, the acquired land, the order for re-determination by applying Factor-2, cannot be passed.

7. Lastly, the only dispute raised before us is that all the co- owners of the land in question are not before us in the instant petition and as such, the disbursement in favour of the petitioners may affect the others.

To take care of the said situation, we only provide that on determination of the compensation by applying Factor-2 as per Section 26(2) of the LARR Act, 2013 including all NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7020/2022 ORDER DATED: 17/01/2024 undefined statutory benefits with respect to the land in question namely Survey No. 182/6, area 8640 sq. mtrs. acquired by NHAI, the question of disbursement of compensation shall be decided by the competent authority by putting notice to all concerned having interest in the land in question.

8. The disbursement of compensation would be independent to the claim of the petitioners herein and the claims of all persons interested in the land in question shall be examined by the competent authority at the time of disbursement.
9. With the above observations and directions, the writ petition stands disposed of.
